vachanas.kannada:
ಕಾಳಗವೆಂಬ ಕಟ್ಟಿದಿರಾದಡೆ,
ಸೋಂಕಿದಡೆ ಬಿಡೆ, ಕರೆದರೆಂದು ಬಿಡೆ.
ವ್ರತ ಹೋದವರು ಸುಳಿಯದಿರಿ.
ಕಂಡಡೆ ಕೊಲುವ ಬಿರಿದು, ಭಿಕಾರಿ ಭೀಮೇಶ್ವರಲಿಂಗವೆ.
vachanas.transliteration:
kāḷagavemba kaṭṭidirādaḍe,
sōṅkidaḍe biḍe, karedarendu biḍe.
vrata hōdavaru suḷiyadiri.
kaṇḍaḍe koluva biridu, bhikāri bhīmēśvaraliṅgave.
vachanas.translation:
If the battle has been joined,
Once engaged, never withdraw; never retreat even if called back.
Do not associate with those who have abandoned their sacred vow.
If you encounter them, destroy them—such is the resolve of Bhikāri Bhīmēśvaraliṅga.

vachanas.kannada:
ಭಿಕಾರಿ ಭಿಕಾರಕ್ಕೆಳಸ.
ಉಣ್ಣಲು ಉಡಲು ಕಾಣದಾತ ಭಿಕಾರಿ.
ತನು ಮೀಸಲು, ಮನ ಮೀಸಲು,
ಬಾಯಿ ಬೋರು ಬೋರು.
ಮರಣವಳಿದುಳಿದಾತ ಭಿಕಾರಿ.
ಸಂಚಲದ ಪಂಚಕರಣಗಳ ತೆಗೆದುಂಡು,
ರುಂಡಮಾಲೆಯ ರಣಮಾಲೆಯ
ಹೆಣಮಾಲೆಯ ಚಾರುಚ್ಚಿದಲ್ಲದೆ
ಭಿಕಾರಿ ಭೀಮೇಶ್ವರಲಿಂಗಕ್ಕೆ ದೂರ ಕಾಣಾ,
ಕರುತಿರುವ ಗೊರವಾ
vachanas.transliteration:
bhikāri bhikārakkeḷasa.
uṇṇalu uḍalu kāṇadāta bhikāri.
tanu mīsalu, mana mīsalu,
bāyi bōru bōru.
maraṇavaḷiduḷidāta bhikāri.
san̄calada pan̄cakaraṇagaḷa tegeduṇḍu,
ruṇḍamāleya raṇamāleya
heṇamāleya cāruccidallade
bhikāri bhīmēśvaraliṅgakke dūra kāṇā,
karutiruva goravā
vachanas.translation:
A beggar is not one who merely lives by begging.
The one who has neither food to eat nor clothing to wear is not the true beggar.
The true beggar has renounced all claim over the body and all claim over the mind.
His mouth remains silent and free from vain speech.
The one who has gone beyond death alone is the true beggar.
Having cast away the five agitating senses,
Wearing not garlands of skulls, nor garlands of battle,
Nor even garlands of corpses for display,
Know that all these are far removed from Bhikāri Bhīmēśvaraliṅga,
O wandering Gorava who merely imagines otherwise.
